v.why: Raising an already large learning rate causes divergence, as in experiments 48, 58 and 60, which show large drops on all three datasets.
Stepping down from a divergent learning rate restores training, as in experiments 49 and 50, which show large gains.
With a tiny learning rate the net is undertrained in 243 epochs, so raising it helps (experiments 41 and 42).
Shallower nets are more stable at high learning rates, as in experiments 93, 98 and 91.
Extra depth amplifies instability when the learning rate is large.
Wider layers produce larger effective updates, which worsens divergence at high learning rates (see experiment 68).
Smaller batches give noisier gradients and more steps at a large learning rate, which destabilises training (experiment 28).
A very strong L2 penalty underfits, so relaxing it helps (experiments 6, 7 and 14).
Extra regularisation on top of an unstable high learning rate hurts further (experiments 12 and 18).
With a small learning rate a deeper net learns faster and is not at risk of divergence (experiments 94 and 97).
